Irish Name: Lá Caille or Lá Bliana Nua
Notes: Added to the public holidays statute in 1974. Most also take time off work for New Year's Eve (Oíche Chinn Bliana).

Date: 1 February or First Monday in February
Notes: First observed in 2023. First Monday of February, or on 1 February if it is a Friday. Co-celebration of the traditional Celtic festival of Imbolc with Saint Brigid's Day.
National day. Became an official public holiday in Ireland in 1903.

Date: Moveable Monday in March or April
Notes: The day after Easter Sunday (Domhnach Cásca). Also coincides with the commemoration of the Easter Rising. The earliest date for Easter Monday is 23 March and the latest date is 26 April.
First observed in 1994. Corresponds with the traditional festival of Bealtaine.

Irish Name: Lá Saoire i mí an Mheithimh
Notes: First observed in 1973. Formerly observed as Whit Monday until 1973.
First observed in 1871. Corresponds with the traditional festival of Lúnasa.

Irish Name: Lá Saoire i mí Dheireadh Fómhair
Notes: First observed in 1977. Corresponds with Halloween and the traditional festival of Samhain.
Most start Christmas celebrations on Christmas Eve (Oíche Nollag), including taking time off work.

Irish Name: Lá Fhéile Stiofáin or Lá an Dreoilín
Notes: The day after Christmas, celebrating the feast day of Saint Stephen. Lá an Dreoilín means Day of the Wren.
